description: Reachability evidence, not a human-usability benchmark. Every trace starts empty and ends on a legal human-policy five.

environment.timingCaveat: Single Node process; does not measure browser worker, UI, mobile-device or human response time.

sampling: 200 consecutive integer seeds per seat beginning 20261009. No games discarded. Same independent greedy tactical policy both seats. Fresh PRNG seed provided for every move. All per-move seeds saved in traces.
limitations: This automated player scans every nearby move and never misses an immediate win or block. Its win rate is not a human win rate.
The short demonstrations are the shortest human-policy victories in the sample, selected to make the tactical ideas easy to inspect. They are not typical game lengths.
Both seats are demonstrably winnable with human-understandable tactics; this is not a measured beginner success rate.

Under the clarified preference to keep the human second unless victory is unrealistic/impossible, recommend human second: simple double-three/open-four tactics produce reproducible full-game wins. Only an actual human five should unlock.

sample.caution: Automated tactical-policy wins demonstrate reachable legal victories, not beginner human usability or a measured human win rate.
sample.policy: Greedy one-placement tactical pattern scoring: immediate wins/blocks, open-four endpoints, forcing four, double/open three, local development. No opponent seed knowledge and no search through opponent responses.

annotation.selection: Shortest human-second victory among the sampled 200 seeds.
tactics: Ply 10 H(7,7) closes one end of the opposing row-7 three; ply 12 H(7,11) blocks its remaining immediate winning gap.
Ply 14 H(6,7) creates two open, broken threes: row 6 at columns 7,8,10 and column 7 at rows 6,7,9.
Panda chooses (8,7), breaking the vertical threat. H(6,9) then fills the horizontal gap, leaving four contiguous stones with two open ends.
Panda correctly blocks (6,6); H(6,11) makes five. This is a standard fork, not a missed immediate block or rules exploit.

annotation.selection: 44 plies, the median winning-game length of the 104 human-second victories.
tactics: Human spends the opening contesting threes and blocks immediate fives at plies 12 and 26.
Ply 30 H(10,3) creates a forcing four; Panda correctly blocks (10,1).
Ply 38 H(7,4) creates a broken column-4 four; Panda correctly fills its winning gap (9,4).
Ply 40 H(5,4) makes another forcing column-4 four; Panda correctly blocks (4,4).
Ply 42 H(7,6) joins H(5,4), H(6,5) and H(8,7) into a diagonal open four. Panda blocks (4,3); H(9,8) wins at the other end.

annotation.selection: 32-ply victory near the lower quartile of second-seat winning lengths.
tactics: Human blocks an immediate five at ply 12, builds an open three at ply 16 and creates a forcing four at ply 18, which Panda correctly blocks.
Ply 28 H(9,12) builds a double open-three threat; after Panda defends, H(9,10) creates a horizontal open four.
Panda correctly blocks (9,8); H(9,13) wins at the other end.
